title: Andrew Barth Feldman is establishing himself as a true multi-hyphenat...
transcript: You probably know Andrew Barth Feldman as an incredibly talented actor and performer, but as it turns out, he's actually a really talented director as well, as he is currently making his directorial debut with obit. It's being staged in one of my favorite venues in the city called East Village Basement. It is literally an East Village apartment that has been converted into a theatre. It's an incredibly intimate space, seating only about 40 audience members, but it is also a space that comes with a lot of limitations because it's a pretty small space. But I was really impressed with how he was able to utilize this space. It never felt restricted, it always felt intentional, seamlessly transitioning from scene to scene, location to location. There's one particular transition into a hospital room that I found really striking and was also enhanced by some really great lighting design by Wheeler Moon. I think this is a really tricky play because it kind of straddles the line between family drama and comedy, and that's a really difficult tightrope to walk tonally. The script is by Trey Everett and follows a man who is about to be a father trying to reconnect with his own father, who he has been estranged from for many years and also, as we quickly find out, has alzheimer's. So, as you can imagine, it can be pretty heavy at times, but does manage to balance it out with just the right amount of levity and They've assembled a really great cast of actors for this as well. Carson Higgins plays our main character and is on stage pretty much the entire show. His character does a lot of direct address towards the audience, and I thought he did a great job at pulling you in and making this character feel very quickly like someone you actually know. We also have Kersten Anderson as his wife, Loren Lester as his father, and Jerusha Cavazos in a role that I won't spoil because she doesn't show up until deep into the play. When she does, oh, boy. Get ready. But I was really impressed with all four of them, and they each get their own moment to shine. It's a very short run, I think only 16 performances and only running through the end of the month. But if you are able to catch it, I would definitely recommend checking it out. And I hope that Andrew does more directing, because I think he shows a ton of promise, and I'm very excited to see what he does next. But for now, Obit is going to be a very strong Broadway Ben recommendation.
